rules.name: monthly_due_date
rules.message: Wages for June 2023 were due before the end of 07 July 2023 (the 7th of the next month).
rules.label: When wages were due

rules.name: pre_code_wages
rules.message: Wages for June 2023 fell due before the Code on Wages started (21 Nov 2025). The older law (Payment of Wages Act) may set a different, shorter time limit for these months, which I haven't verified. Talk to free legal aid (15100) soon.
rules.label: Older months: check with a lawyer

rules.name: where_to_claim
rules.message: You (or your union) can file a claim before the wage authority. For banks, railways, telecom, mines, insurance and central PSUs this is the Central Government's authority; for other employers it is your State labour department. It can order up to ten times the claim as compensation and recovers unpaid amounts like land revenue. The employer has to prove they paid you.
rules.label: Where to claim

rules.name: amount
rules.message: Unpaid wages: 1 month(s) x Rs 28,000 = Rs 28,000 (before any lawful deductions; HRA and overtime also count as wages for payment).
rules.label: Amount

answer.summary: Your employer in Jaipur did not pay your June 2023 salary of Rs 28,000. You can file a wage claim. The law says your salary was due by 7 July 2023. You can file a claim before the labour authority. The employer must prove they paid you. You can also get free legal help by calling 15100.

claims.text: You are an employee because you work for wages under your employer.
Wages include your basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance.
Monthly wages must be paid before the 7th day of the next month.
The employer must prove they paid you if you claim non-payment.
The wage authority can order up to ten times the claim as compensation.

support.text: You are an employee because you work for wages under your employer.
support.reason: The law text defines 'employee' as any person employed on wages by an establishment to do work for hire or reward, which directly supports the sentence that being employed on wages by an employer makes one an employee.

support.text: Wages include your basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance.
support.reason: The law text explicitly includes basic pay, dearness allowance, and retaining allowance in the definition of wages, which directly supports the sentence.

support.text: Monthly wages must be paid before the 7th day of the next month.
support.reason: The law text states that for monthly basis employment, wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month, which directly supports the sentence.

support.text: The employer must prove they paid you if you claim non-payment.
support.reason: The law text explicitly states that 'the burden to prove that the said dues have been paid shall be on the employer' when a claim is filed for non-payment, which directly supports the sentence.

support.text: The wage authority can order up to ten times the claim as compensation.
support.reason: The law text states that compensation 'may extend to ten times of the claim determined', which directly supports the sentence that the wage authority can order up to ten times the claim as compensation.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: My employer, [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for payment of unpaid wages

I was employed with you at a monthly wage of Rs 28,000. My wages for June 2023 have not been paid.

I request you to pay the unpaid amount of Rs 28,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter, to my bank account [FILL: account details].

If the amount is not paid, I intend to file a claim before the authority under the Code on Wages, 2019, which may also award compensation, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]
escalation_reasons: validator: answer still failed after one retry; failing sentences removed
draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in your offer letter, salary slip, or the company's registered office on the MCA website (mca.gov.in).
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Code on Wages, 2019, s.17(1)-(4) (Time limit for payment of wages); Code on Wages, 2019, s.69 (Repeal of Payment of Wages Act and Minimum Wages Act, with savings); Code on Wages, 2019, s.45(1)-(6) (Claims authority, compensation, recovery and time limit); Code on Wages, 2019, s.59 (Burden of proof on employer); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(d) (Central or State Government: whose authority applies); Code on Wages, 2019, s.2(y) (main part, clauses (a)-(j)) (What counts as "wages")
